newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed mixed in a session highlighted by selling of the 10-year benchmark.
Dealers said a Dutch institution sold the 5.75 percent February 2007 state loan to switch into the 10-year German Bund, which is offering a significant yield pick-up.
"We have seen good selling again in the 10-year sector. Domestics are getting out of Holland into foreign assets," said one dealer.
"It's a process that's likely to continue," he added, echoing the view that the 10-year benchmark is overvalued when it is yielding less than 5.50 percent.
The Dutch 10-year yield differential to Germany ended at -9 basis points, -15 less than a week ago.

The yield spread in the 30-year sector has narrowed even more dramatically as investors switched out of guilders into the new German benchmark issued earlier this week."We have seen a lot of demand for the German 30 year," the dealer said.
The 30-year spread ended at -10 basis points, from -17 on June 30.
He said the Dutch 2023 bond was well bid as short sellers took profits on the recent steepening of the Dutch yield curve between 10 and 30 years.
Another dealer said foreign investors also sold Dutch longer paper, some switching into nearer-dated bonds to shorten duration.
"Some people think the market's looking a bit toppish," he said.
He added: "With the U.S. holiday (for Independence Day), it's been a pretty tame afternoon."
